Questions / Dad

How do I stay present as Dad?

Attention. Patience. The next ordinary moment.

Being Dad asks something different of me from building a system or explaining an idea. I want to be someone my children can turn to: ready to listen, willing to learn, and responsible for the way I use my authority.

Follow the questions ↓

A question to practise, not a finished answer.

Dad

Care has to become something they can experience.

Good intentions do not make me present. I have to make time, notice when I am distracted, and listen without deciding too quickly what someone needs. These are commitments I want to practise, not a claim that I have got parenting figured out.

Where the question becomes concrete.

Attention

Am I listening, or already preparing my answer?

I want to make room for what my children are actually telling me, including feelings I cannot immediately fix. Sometimes the next good thing is to put the task down and stay.

Explore listening →

Authority

Can I set a boundary without making love feel conditional?

Being responsible includes saying no when something is unsafe. I want the reason to be understandable, and the relationship to remain a place of care even when we disagree.

Explore restraint →

Repair

Can I say I was wrong without making them comfort me?

An apology should name what I did and be followed by a change. My children should not have to carry the work of protecting my image of myself.

Explore repair →

Growing room

Am I helping them become themselves?

I can offer support, experience and protection while leaving room for their own interests and judgment. The question is what helps them grow, rather than what makes my plans easier.

Explore care →

Another side of the same life.

These commitments meet in one life. Each brings a different question into focus.
